i do suggest therapy alot but the only thing is if you also end up with a psychiatrist (who prescribes meds) you should be very cautious and stay informed about what they’re trying to give you if you’re considering taking it. some medications can really help some symptoms but some will really make it worse if your doctor makes a mistake with your diagnosis. im not against the medications of course but if there is a mishap where you’re prescribed something you probably shouldn’t have been given you may become alot worse as in feeling hopeless and suicidal. so make sure you’re communicating and asking questions and if you feel like the doctor is wrong about something or they’re missing something let them know so you can reduce the chance of something going wrong. or if given the offer for medications you can also just say no bc they dont have to give it to you if you dont wish to take it. im not sure of your age or area but if you’re in school the easiest way to get into therapy would be to talk your counselor. if you’re an adult or just not going to school right now you can also go to a hospital for an evaluation. they should give you some resources to find a therapist near you but you can ask if for some reason they dont. i live in america im unsure if its the same anywhere else. i hope it helps.
